patients.summary: Graduate student with generalized anxiety disorder on sertraline and as-needed alprazolam, and migraine without aura on as-needed sumatriptan, who joins in 2022. IBS-D is diagnosed in June 2024; in December 2025 she is seen in an outside ED for a benzodiazepine overdose of her own alprazolam after a breakup, which the practice learns of from her and whose record arrives late. Alprazolam is stopped and she starts counseling.

conditions.label: Generalized anxiety disorder
conditions.note: Diagnosed at prior primary care office

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth as needed for anxiety. Max 2 tablets per day
Take 1 tablet by mouth at onset of migraine as needed

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, low MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

22F, starting a graduate program this fall, transferring care from her prior primary care office. Wants one doctor she can reach. Records release signed today.

ANXIETY: dx GAD around 2019 at her old office. Sertraline 50 mg daily since then, says it took the edge off within a couple of months and she has not wanted to change it. Alprazolam 0.25 mg tabs as needed, which she says she uses "a few times a month," mostly before presentations or when she can't settle at night. Never more than 2 in a day. Not in counseling currently, did some in college. No SI, no history of self-harm.

HEADACHES: migraines since about 15. Unilateral throbbing, light and noise bother her, sometimes nauseated, no visual aura or weakness. Maybe 1-3 a month, more around deadlines. Sumatriptan 50 mg works within an hour most times; rarely needs a second dose. Has never taken a daily preventive.

PMH: as above. PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
MEDS: sertraline 50 daily; alprazolam 0.25 prn (max 2/day); sumatriptan 50 prn.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FH: mother with GAD. Father with migraines. Maternal grandmother had IBS.
SH: grad student, lives off campus. Never smoker. 1-2 drinks a week socially. No drugs.

ROS: negative except as above. Bowels regular, no GI complaints.

EXAM: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, pleasant, a bit fidgety. HEENT unremarkable, fundi sharp. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro: CN II-XII intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal. Skin without rash.

GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. GAD, stable on sertraline 50. Continue. Discussed that alprazolam is a backup, not a plan; small fills, I will check the state PMP with each refill. She is fine with that.
2. Migraine without aura, episodic, sumatriptan effective. Reviewed the 2-dose daily max and not more than ~9 days/month. Mentioned serotonin symptoms to watch for with sertraline plus triptan, low risk at these doses.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, one-time HIV and HCV, GC/CT urine NAAT today. Pap per old records, will confirm when they come. Flu and COVID booster next month.

RTC for a physical in about a year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Hannah - all of Wednesday's bloodwork looks fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are normal, and the HIV, hepatitis C, chlamydia and gonorrhea tests were all negative. Nothing to follow up on. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Prior primary care records received by fax, 23 pages, scanned to chart.

Summary abstracted by MA:
- Generalized anxiety disorder, diagnosed spring 2019. Sertraline 50 mg daily started at that time. Alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed added later for breakthrough anxiety, small quantities.
- Migraine without aura since mid-teens, sumatriptan 50 mg as needed.
- Wisdom teeth extraction 2018.
- Cervical cytology 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Immunizations: HPV series completed in adolescence. Tdap 2021.
- Allergies: none known.

No outstanding items.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and COVID bivalent booster. No fever today, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, COVID bivalent IM R deltoid. Observed 15 min without issue. VIS given. Left with an ice pack for the next class.

documents.title: Refill request - alprazolam
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pharmacy fax for alprazolam 0.25 mg. Last fill per PMP was mid-August from prior office, #20. No other controlled fills. Routed to PCP.

PCP: PMP reviewed. OK #20, no refills. Finals stretch, she says she's using it maybe twice a week right now.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient in her apartment, ID confirmed.

S: Migraines picked up in January, maybe 4 in the month, back to 1-2 the last few weeks. Same pattern as always, no aura, no new features. Sumatriptan still works. She thinks it was sleep and too much coffee while writing a paper. No neuro symptoms between headaches.

O: Appears well on video, speech fluent, face symmetric.

A/P: Episodic migraine without aura, transient uptick, below the range where I'd push a preventive. Sleep regularity, caffeine before noon, keep a headache log. Sumatriptan 50 refilled #9 x 2. If she is regularly over 4 a month we will talk about prophylaxis.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 3:00 follow-up. Called, voicemail. Left message to rebook. Patient texted back she lost track of the day with a lab deadline, rebooked as video 6/7.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, she is home. Apologized for missing last time.

Semester ended OK. Anxiety "about normal for me." Sleeping 7 hours most nights. Takes sertraline every day, no side effects she notices. Alprazolam maybe 3-4 times a month now, one at a time. Headaches back to baseline. No low mood, no SI.

A/P: GAD stable. Continue sertraline 50 mg. Alprazolam as is, last fill in April per PMP, use remains light. Brought up counseling again as the better long-term tool, she will look at the student counseling list this summer. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Turning 24 at the end of the month. Second year of her program. No new concerns.

Interval: anxiety steady on sertraline, alprazolam a few times a month. Migraines 1-2/month, sumatriptan effective. Never started counseling, says time. No ED or urgent care visits. Bowels normal.

Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily; alprazolam 0.25 mg prn (max 2/day); sumatriptan 50 mg prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/week, no drugs. Exercises by walking to campus.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck without nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Extremities without edema. Skin no concerning lesions. Neuro grossly normal. Mood good, affect bright.

GAD-7 5. PHQ-9 2. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
- Healthy 23F. GAD and migraine stable on current regimen, no changes.
- GC/CT urine NAAT today (under 25).
- Pap next due 2024 (last 2021).
- Flu and updated COVID vaccine given today.
- RTC 1 year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Test result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Hannah, your urine tests from Wednesday's physical were negative. No action needed. - nursing

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, could you send more sumatriptan? I'm down to one and I'm flying home next week. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Refill request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent #9 with 2 refills to your usual pharmacy. Safe travels, and enjoy the break.
